Appendix B: Embedded Behavioral Economics Experiment The researchers incorporated a behavioral economics experiment into the survey to test the influence of framing information on participants’ responses. The experiment is based on construal level theory, which describes psychological distance and the extent to which a person’s thinking is abstract or concrete (Trope & Liberman, 2010). Research shows that the more abstract an idea or action, the less likely a person is to act on it and the greater the psychological distance, which refers to the degree of cognitive separation between a person and something else. Priming, a technique in which the introduction of one stimulus influences how people respond to a subsequent stimulus, and framing, which refers to the way information is presented, have been proven to affect psychological distance and decision-making (Flusberg et al., 2024; Henderson & Wakslak, 2010; Zhu et al., 2017).
